text:
sarah_support: customer reports requests to their private Redwood endpoint time out from their app but succeed from an EC2 bastion in the same subnet. TL;DR: suspected firewall/NACL issue.

mike_oncall: can you paste the curl output and the subnet/NACL IDs? any TLS errors or just hangs?

sarah_support: here's reproduce: from app container -> curl -v https://10.0.51.12:8443/v1/generate  (timed out after 60s). from bastion -> curl -v https://10.0.51.12:8443/v1/generate (200 OK). No TLS cert errors.

alex_infra: interesting — same subnet but different path to internet/NAT? if app runs in private subnet behind NAT gateway, return ports matter. do you have NACLs on that subnet?

sarah_support: yes subnet-0a1b2c3d uses acl-0f1e2d3c. customer shared NACL rules below.

sarah_support: ```
RULE 100: ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0
RULE 110: DENY ALL ALL 0.0.0.0/0
```

jess_prodeng: That DENY ALL is likely default deny catching ephemeral return traffic. Reminder: NACLs are stateless — you must allow both inbound and outbound for response ports.

alex_infra: exactly. common failure: inbound 8443 allowed, but outbound ephemeral ports (eg 32768-61000 or 1024-65535) are DENY so instance can't send back TCP ACKs to the client. bastion likely uses a different subnet/NACL that allows ephemeral.

sarah_support: customer confirmed they had a very restrictive outbound on that NACL. they only allowed 443 outbound.

mike_oncall: quick test commands we asked them to run:
- nc -vz 10.0.51.12 8443 (from app container)
- tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp and port 8443' (on instance)
- sudo aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids acl-0f1e2d3c | jq '.NetworkAcls[0].Entries'

sarah_support: their nc from app: "Connection timed out". tcpdump on instance shows SYN arriving from client but no SYN-ACK leaving instance (we saw SYN only).

infra-bot: reminder: NACLs are evaluated in order and are stateless. For TCP you must allow the ephemeral port range on both inbound and outbound to permit connection establishment.

jess_prodeng: recommended quick fix: add outbound rule allowing ephemeral range (32768-61000) to 0.0.0.0/0 and mirror inbound if you rely on client-initiated ephemeral ports. If you want conservative: allow 1024-65535.

alex_infra: example AWS CLI to add entry (adjust rule number):
```bash
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0f1e2d3c \
  --rule-number 115 --protocol tcp --port-range From=32768,To=61000 \
  --egress --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --rule-action allow
```

mike_oncall: note: if you're using an NLB that preserves client source IP, this is a must. If you use ALB (proxy) the source will be the ALB and different behavior applies.

sarah_support: customer applied outbound allow for 32768-61000 and removed the blanket DENY. retested and app->curl now returns 200 within 200ms.

jess_prodeng: great. follow-ups: 1) add a short doc blurb about NACL statefulness + ephemeral ports to the private deployment checklist, 2) suggest using security groups for stateful filters where possible (SGs are stateful so less error-prone).

alex_infra: also add a quick diagnostic snippet to the KB: tcpdump showing SYN only is a tell for return traffic blocked.

mike_oncall: marking resolved on the ticket. customer asked if TLS certs could be to blame — we confirmed certs were fine because curl -v from bastion showed proper handshake.

sarah_support: :white_check_mark: resolved — adding notes to incident thread and KB.
